globalAffineFamilyBound.classification: formal exact global lower-and-upper bound for the complete affine family
globalAffineFamilyBound.lowerProof: the exact Krawczyk root has both active columns equal to one, all 242 inactive sector envelopes are below one, and its radius lies strictly above r_L
globalAffineFamilyBound.upperProof: the eliminated feasibility theorem excludes every c>0 and lambda>=0 at r_U; radius monotonicity excludes all larger radii
globalAffineFamilyBound.whatRemains: the width-10^-40 enclosure does not by itself identify the local KKT root with the unique global maximizer as an exact real number

globalExclusion.monotonicRadiusExtension: B and Z have positive coefficients and strictly increase in r; therefore no radius at or above r_U is feasible
globalExclusion.proof: outside [c_L,c_U], U0>1 or M0>1 with M1>=0. Inside, the three-root derivative theorem shows that E can attain a maximum only at c_L, c_U, or the second derivative-root box. The endpoint values and every Bernstein coefficient on that box are negative, so E<0 throughout the remaining domain.

aboveUpper.proof: M1 is strictly increasing in log(c), is positive at c_U, and the R0.50 global theorem gives M0>1 at this radius; hence B=M0+alpha*M1>1 for every c>=c_U

belowLower.proof: T0 is strictly increasing in log(c), is negative at c_L, and U0(c_L)>1; hence U0>1 for every c<=c_L

inactiveSectorTheorem.proof: r, c^q, and each affine ratio are bounded termwise at exact box endpoints. Positive coefficients make the envelopes simultaneous. Fixed-charge convex endpoints, the exceptional all-degree theorems, and the large-charge parity theorem exhaust every inactive sector.

krawczykCertificate.theorem: the exact Krawczyk image K(x0,X) is strictly contained in the interior of X; therefore F=G=H=0 has exactly one zero in X

localMaximumCertificate.classification: formal exact strict constrained local-maximum theorem
localMaximumCertificate.proof: at the certified root H=0 is the c-alpha stationarity determinant. The exact interval multipliers in grad(r)=mu*grad(F)+nu*grad(G) are positive, LICQ holds, and tau^T(mu Hess(F)+nu Hess(G)) tau>0. Since Hess(r)=0, the Lagrangian is strictly negative on the one-dimensional critical tangent space.
